units.title: Forecast: easing, high pressure building
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Today: westerly 4 or 5, decreasing 3 later. Showers dying out, then a fine afternoon. Sea moderate, becoming slight. Swell 2 m this morning on east coasts, easing to around 1 m by tomorrow evening. Max 9 C. Tonight: clear and cold, light winds, a ground frost inland. Outlook: high pressure building; mist and fog patches possible on coasts at dawn later this week.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. Normal timetabled services resume this morning. Our relief vessel will carry out sea trials off Weyhaven this afternoon. If the trials and the forecast allow, we have offered the Coastguard a daylight sailing to Kittering Holm at first light in two days' time. This remains provisional and will be confirmed or cancelled on this page. Regular passengers: timetables may change on that morning.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard Marrow Sound. Planning for a daylight transfer from Kittering Holm continues. A provisional operation at first light in two days' time is being assessed with Sound Lines, subject to vessel trials, the swell at the east dock and visibility. A final decision will be taken early on the morning itself. Mariners are asked to keep clear of the Holm's east approaches that morning. This notice does not confirm the operation.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Gilliver Village Hall will remain open as an information point, now until 22:00, with thanks to the volunteers. Recycling collections missed in the gale on Rope Walk, Quay Lane and the Gilliver harbour front will be made tomorrow. The Brackwater junction temporary lights have been reset. For anything about Kittering Holm, please refer to the Coastguard's notices.

units.title: Kittering Holm: a clarification
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. We have received a number of calls asking whether we can 'turn the power back on' at Kittering Holm. The island is not connected to our network and never has been. Any lighting there runs from on-site generation. We have no information about the site. Thank you to the many callers who also asked after our linemen after the gale: everyone is fine.

units.title: Ferry company's Holm plan hinges on the weather
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines has offered its relief vessel for a daylight sailing to Kittering Holm, the Courier understands, provided sea trials this afternoon go well and the swell at the island's east dock falls below the limit set for a landing. The earliest window being discussed is first light in two days' time.

units.author: courier
units.text: A briefing for volunteer crew was held at the Port Ammet terminal this morning. One volunteer described the plan as 'simple on paper': approach in daylight, come alongside the Holm's timber pier near the top of the tide, take off whoever is waiting at the dock end, and leave. 'The hard part is everything that isn't on paper,' they said.

units.author: courier
units.text: Forecasters say high pressure will bring calm seas by then, but also the chance of fog at dawn. The Coastguard said a final decision would be taken on the morning itself, and that it would not 'promise families a time and then break it'. It again asked people not to gather at slipways.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services has not added to its statement. Ardent Vale Holdings has still not responded. A Gilliver resident who has kept a lamp in her window every night of her life said she had 'put another one in, for luck, or for manners, whichever is needed'.

units.title: Gilliver keeps its lamps lit
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:00 ST. On the Gilliver front tonight nearly every window facing the Holm has a lamp in it, many of them two. Nobody we spoke to would say who started it. 'It's what we do,' said one man walking his dog. 'It's not a vigil. It's just so they know the house is awake.'

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:40 ST. Sound Lines says the relief vessel's sea trials this afternoon were 'satisfactory'. The provisional first-light sailing is still under review. The company again asked people not to come to the terminal or to Gilliver slipway on the morning, as the vessel will not be taking passengers or press.

units.title: Notice: reconciliation in progress
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Grieve Land Services payroll. Contract ref: KH-30. Reconciliation status: in progress. Expected completion: within 10 working days. No action is required from you at this time. Your statement will be issued to the address held on file. Scheduled maintenance: the payroll portal will be unavailable from 22:00 to 23:30 tonight. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Payment received, thank you
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, thank you. We have received your monthly premium for policy LM-PA-40217. Your cover continues uninterrupted. Peace of mind, every month. If your circumstances have changed, including your place of work, please let us know so we can make sure you're properly protected. Lyle Mutual: here for the long run. This is an automated message.

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello again. A short update, in case it's any use, though I know it may not reach you or be welcome. 1) Sound Lines has offered its relief boat for a first-light sailing, if the weather allows. 2) The Coastguard won't confirm it until the morning itself. 3) Grieve and Ardent Vale still haven't answered. I've stopped writing 'declined to comment' and started writing 'did not respond', which is more accurate. Nell Ashdown

units.title: steadier
units.author: sam
units.text: I'm steadier today, I think. I've decided to be useful, so I've been to the shops for Mum and walked the dog twice and rung the ferry people only once, which they appreciated. the radio says there might be a boat. might. I've written it on the calendar in pencil. the kid asked if you'd be back for the end-of-term play and I said I didn't know, which was the first honest thing I've said all week. love, S x

units.title: Sea trials
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Heard from the Weyhaven yard that the relief boat's trials went fine. Engineer on board is supposed to be the fussy sort, which is the sort you want. Forget what I said about Corran, I shouldn't have sent it. Different job, different weather, different everything. I'm driving to Gilliver tomorrow night so I'm there if anything happens. Not that I'll be any use. I'll bring biscuits for the hall.

units.title: Tell him
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: I'm sorry I keep writing. The woman at the Coastguard said I could leave a message for the crew 'in case it can be passed on' and I didn't know what to say, so I said tell Tomas his sister is fine. Then I thought of all the things I should have said instead. It's the same message though. If he's with you, tell him I'm fine. Ana

units.title: Gilliver window lamp (custom)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The keeping of a lamp in a window facing the Sound after dusk is recorded in Gilliver since at least the 1880s (Courier, village column). Explanations offered by residents vary: for boats, for luck, for the dead, 'for manners'. No single origin is attested [citation needed]. Editor's note, this week: the custom is once again widely observed along the Gilliver front, many houses now keeping two lamps.

units.title: Lights Board survey, Kittering Holm (1953): Appendix C, landing
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Appendix C. Landing. The east jetty (timber, 19th c.) is serviceable for a launch at half tide and above, in a sea state not exceeding slight. Below half tide on springs the approach dries and the jetty is unusable. A landing barge ramp would be required for any permanent station. Party landed on 11 of 14 scheduled days, the remainder lost to swell. Party taken off each day before dusk, as requested.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Who were the lamps for, do you think? Mr and Mrs R. (b. 1910, 1913). Mr R.: 'For them on the road.' Mrs R.: 'Don't be daft, there's no road on the Holm.' Mr R.: 'I never said the Holm.' [pause] Mrs R.: 'He means the shore road at Carrow. His mother was from Carrow. They're all strange there.' [both laugh]

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day nine, and the last. Boatman Creed came at dawn rather than noon and said we must be off by the turn, the glass falling, though it is the steadiest glass I have seen all week. I did not argue. Packed the press and specimens in twenty minutes. Lists complete except for mammals, of which I record none. (Sketch: the jetty from the boat, the hazel behind it, untouched.)

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr. 28th. No felling. Roll at dusk 11 men. The boat come at last at noon and nine went over on her with there tools, Coad cursing them from the jetty and then helping them load. I paid them in full from the box. He has told the rest of us the agent's boat will come for the last of us 'when the sea allows'. I have entered that, as I enter everything.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Feb. 23. 00:00 wind S 3, fog, vis. 200 yds. Fog signal sounding. 02:00 fog thickening. 03:40 lamp trimmed and burning well. Remarks: Rowe reports a lamp seen on the Holm side, low, about the bearing of the old timber jetty, where there has been nobody these ten years. Fog too thick to be sure of it. Perhaps a boat. E.S.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 05:00 swell reading as promised: 2.1 m, and the period's down to 9 seconds. Pressure 1019 and rising, wind W 11 knots. Sky clearing from the west, Venus out over the Holm at half five as if nothing had happened. By tomorrow evening I'd expect under a metre at the point. Dew point dropping too, so watch for fog at dawn the day after.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Summary for anyone arriving late. Facts: a beacon on the Holm, acknowledged. Lights on the island every night, seen by several people independently. A contractor that won't say who it left, and an owner that won't say anything. A ferry company and a Coastguard planning a daylight sailing that depends on swell and fog. Unknown: how many people, how they are, what they've been told. That's the honest list, and it's long enough.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Added. Sound Lines: sea trials this afternoon; 'a daylight sailing to Kittering Holm at first light in two days' time', provisional, 'will be confirmed or cancelled on this page'. Coastguard: 'a final decision will be taken early on the morning itself'. Council: Gilliver Hall open till 22:00. Sound Power: the Holm is not on its network and never was. Pell.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Fine. But if they get there and it's an empty camp and a beacon on a stick, I want an apology from every one of you who's been writing these lads' obituaries for a week.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update from our house: the kids have stopped asking whether the island people are 'dead' and started asking whether they've got enough food, which feels like progress. The middle one has drawn a boat with an enormous lamp on the front. School is collecting tins for Gilliver Hall, though I don't think the hall can post them to an island.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: If they get there and it's an empty camp, Cal, I'll happily apologise to anyone for anything, because it would mean everyone's somewhere warm already. I don't think that's what anyone here is afraid of. And nobody on this thread has written an obituary. Pell would have removed it within the minute.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: That will be Fly, from the Pask farm at the top of the coast road. She goes walkabout in a gale every year and always ends up near the chippy. I have rung Mrs Pask and she is coming down for her. Thank you, young man, that was kind of you. Maud

units.title: Ferry timetable on the morning of the Holm sailing?
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Practical one. If the Holm boat goes at first light, does the 07:10 still run? I've a delivery on Lisle at eight and I'd rather not be the van holding up a rescue. Also the Brackwater jct lights have been 'reset', according to the council, which means they now go red in both directions at once.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions: why first light 'in two days' and not tomorrow, when the sea's calming? A source says the delay is so Ardent Vale can get their own boat out there first and 'tidy up'. I'm not saying that's true. I'm saying somebody should ask. Do your research.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Gil, the Coastguard and Sound Lines have both given the reason in writing: sea trials today, and the swell at the east dock. If your source has evidence otherwise, send it to the Courier, who can check it, not here. Further unsourced claims about a private boat will be removed. Pell.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Evening summary. Swell 1.4 m, wind WNW 6 knots and dying, pressure 1027. Clear sky, already down to 3 C at nine. This is fog weather for the morning after next if the wind goes calm: cold air over a warmer sea, clear nights. I hate saying it, because I know what morning people are watching. It may burn off by eight. It may not.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Spoke to Kerris on the 17:30 for about four minutes, which is the longest she's ever spoken to me. She said the trials went well and then she said 'don't put that on the forum', so I'm not putting the rest on the forum. I will say I've been unfair about the welfare review business. I'm sorry for that.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Clear tonight. Went down the slip at nine. Lights on the Holm, three I'm sure of, maybe a fourth at the cabin end. They didn't move tonight. Two in my own window, one each side of the clock. Wife says it's daft. She lit the second one.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: ha, Fly. she ate two sausages and a battered sausage. Mrs Pask came in an old pickup and gave me a fiver, which I put in the hall tin. also, I did the slipway thing once, I've said that, and I'm not doing anything stupid this week, before anyone asks.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Volunteer briefing this morning at the terminal. I'll skipper the relief vessel if the sailing is approved. Sea trials at three. I won't put the plan on here, except to say it's daylight, it's simple, and we will turn round if the dock isn't safe. That's not a lack of nerve, that's how you get everyone home. Briefed, signed, back to the night boat tonight.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour notice, for information. On the morning of any approved relief sailing, the Gilliver slipway and the north pontoon will be closed to the public from 05:00 until the harbour office reopens them. This is so the area is clear if the vessel comes in here. Please do not gather on the harbour wall. Thank you. HM

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Back from trials. She steers like a wardrobe but she's sound. That's all I'm saying, because Ewan from Lisle will put it on the Sound Board otherwise. Tomorrow I sleep. Then we see what the fog does, and I don't think anybody in this harbour can tell us that.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Ladders went on the relief boat this afternoon, the good ones. Lads, I'll have the chandlery open from five on the morning in case anyone needs anything for the boat: flasks, lines, batteries. Not for watching. If you come to watch I'll give you a mop and you can do the floor.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Kennel update: Clover went home to her family today, wagging. Moss still won't go down the back corridor, though he did put one paw over the line tonight and then looked at me like he'd done me a favour. Someone asked if I'd get the vents checked again. I did. A wasp nest, empty. He's still not having it.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: weekly tidy. Thank you all for keeping the Marrow Sound threads kind. I've removed two posts this week that named people on the island; no warnings, just don't. Lots of you have said you're lighting a lamp for them, wherever you are. That's allowed. Water, snacks, stretch. Tell us about your shift.

units.title: Quiet lift, long view
units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Quiet lift tonight, precast panels for the hospital extension. From sixty metres the city looks like somebody spilled a box of amber beads. I've kept my threads short and easy since the other one, which I'm still sorry about. Someone on the ground crew asked if I'd heard about the island people up north. I said I had. We both looked at the river for a bit.

units.title: B corridor, slow run
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: B corridor, slow run. A&E had a meeting at handover about 'a possible transfer from an island, date unknown, numbers unknown', which is exactly as much as the radio knows. Sister has made up trolleys with extra blankets and labelled them 'island, maybe'. The vending machine on B has started giving two hot chocolates for one press. Telling nobody but you lot.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Update: Control has borrowed a boat. Not to go anywhere, he says, just to 'have one ready'. It's on a trailer in his drive, it's eleven feet long and it has a hole in it. He rang me at two to tell me about the hole. Patrol, nil found, except a hedgehog by the trolley bay, who I've named Control.

units.title: Bookshop, late
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: The bookshop stayed open till two again. Six people came in over the evening and none of them bought anything, which is exactly right. One woman read the same page of a sea novel for an hour. A man from Gilliver said every window there has a lamp now and asked if I had a book about lamps. I found him one about lighthouses. He said that would do.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ivy that sketch is genuinely nice, i've made it my lock screen. the bike lock is mine, sorry, i'll get it. lights on, stairs normal, i counted 38 steps on the way up tonight for old times' sake and tobin can check my working. hope that island lot have their lights on too.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Checked. Two flights, 6 to 8: 19 per flight, n=38. Correct. For the record, I said I had stopped counting and I have; this is jordie's count, not mine. Also, for whoever is waiting on news from the island: a working light and a known number of steps are not nothing. I hope they have both.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: A very fine recording of a roof. In 1962 I recorded the old Port Ammet pier in a gale on a borrowed machine, and the halyards sounded just like this, though the tape has since gone a little soft. I find wind on its own a great comfort, being nothing but itself. Regards, Ned

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I put arrows on hollis's analysis and all the arrows point at things he's already named, which is a first. (typo: hollis's, I always get that wrong.) slightly off topic, school is doing a lamp-making workshop with year sevens this week, jam jars and tealights. the kids asked who for. I said anyone who needs one.
